issues.legal_issue: A writ court cannot order a tenant’s eviction in a manner that bypasses statutory protections and procedures that may apply to the tenancy.
material_facts: A landlord sought eviction after the tenant’s lease expired and the landlord refused a request to extend it.
The tenant claimed benefits under the applicable tenant-protection law, including compensation and a possible right to seek purchase of the land.
The High Court ordered eviction in a writ proceeding by relying on an earlier decision, without considering the claimed statutory protections or requiring proceedings under the applicable law.
issues.conclusion: The eviction direction was set aside. The landlord may pursue the remedies available through the appropriate proceedings, where the tenant’s entitlement to statutory protection can be determined; the Supreme Court did not decide that entitlement on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 9 of the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921 provide benefits that cannot be diluted through a writ proceeding. Where their application or the tenant’s entitlement is disputed, it can be more effectively determined in proceedings taken under that Act. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dolly Das did not justify bypassing those procedures, because the provisions corresponding to Sections 3 and 9 were not under consideration there.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_eviction_order and landlord_used_writ_to_seek_eviction and tenant_claimed_statutory_protection and statutory_entitlement_requires_determination_in_proper_proceedings

predicates.appeal_from_writ_eviction_order: A party appealed an order directing eviction in a writ proceeding.
predicates.landlord_used_writ_to_seek_eviction: A landlord sought to evict a tenant through a writ proceeding rather than the applicable ordinary statutory process.
predicates.tenant_claimed_statutory_protection: The tenant claimed that a law gave it protections relevant to eviction.
predicates.statutory_entitlement_requires_determina: The tenant’s entitlement to the claimed protections could be determined in proceedings provided by the applicable law.

issues.definition: When an eviction direction made in a writ proceeding is appealed, the landlord used that proceeding to seek eviction, the tenant claimed statutory protection, and proper proceedings are needed to determine entitlement, the direction is set aside for proper proceedings.

issues.legal_issue: A court must compare the material facts and legal context before applying an earlier decision as a precedent.
material_facts: The High Court relied on Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dolly Das to order eviction.
The earlier decision did not consider tenant protections corresponding to Sections 3 and 9 of the applicable tenant-protection law.
The High Court did not consider the effect of those protections before applying the earlier decision.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not justify the eviction order because the legal and factual context differed, and the High Court had not considered that difference.
issues.legal_principle: Judgments are not statutes, and judicial observations must be read in their context. A precedent should be applied only after assessing how its facts and legal setting fit the case at hand; even a significant difference may change the result. The Court relied on the contextual cautions expressed in London Graving Dock Co. Ltd. v. Horton, Home Office v. Dorset Yacht Co., Herrington v. British Railways Board, and the cited observations of Lord Denning on distinguishing cases.

predicates.precedent_based_adjudication: A court relied on an earlier decision to resolve a later case.
predicates.precedent_material_facts_not_compared: The court did not assess whether the material facts and legal setting of the earlier decision matched the later case.
predicates.current_case_has_materially_different_le: The later case involved legal protections that were not considered in the earlier decision.

issues.definition: When a court relies on an earlier decision without comparing its material facts, and the later case has materially different legal protections, the earlier decision cannot control without contextual comparison.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s statutory option to seek purchase of land in an eviction proceeding is a conditional privilege that requires a court to determine the minimum land needed for the tenant’s convenient enjoyment.
material_facts: The tenant occupied leased land on which a petrol pump had been set up.
The tenant claimed the benefit of a statutory right to seek purchase of land and compensation for a building or improvements upon eviction.
The High Court had not considered the statutory procedure for determining whether, and to what extent, the tenant required the land for convenient enjoyment.
The Supreme Court left the application of the statutory provisions and the tenant’s entitlement to be decided in appropriate proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The purchase option is not an absolute or vested right. When a tenant makes an application under the statutory procedure, the court must inquire into the minimum extent of land needed for convenient enjoyment; it may refuse purchase relief if the tenant does not need any part of the land. The tenant may also be entitled to compensation for qualifying buildings and improvements on ejectment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 9 of the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921 govern compensation on ejectment and the court-supervised purchase option. Under Section 9, the court must determine the minimum extent needed for the tenant’s convenient enjoyment and may grant purchase relief only to that extent. Swami Motor Transport (P) Ltd. v. Sri Sankaraswamigal Mull holds that the option is a statutory right to purchase, not an interest in the property. P. Ananthakrishnan Nair v. Dr. G. Ramakrishnan is cited on the operation of these protections. The Court noted Hindustan Petroleum Corporation v. Raja D.V. Appa Rao Bahadur and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. P. Kesavan as matters whose application could be considered in appropriate proceedings.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_under_tenant_protect: A landlord initiated an eviction proceeding to which a tenant-protection law applies.
predicates.tenant_applies_for_purchase: The tenant applied for an order requiring the landlord to sell land to the tenant.
predicates.tenant_claims_land_for_convenient_use: The tenant claimed that some or all of the land was needed for the convenient enjoyment of the tenant’s use of the property.

issues.definition: When a tenant applies to purchase land in an eviction proceeding governed by tenant-protection law and claims the land for convenient use, the court must inquire into the minimum extent needed for that use.
